question.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(a<X<b)=P(\frac{a-\mu }{\sigma }<Z<\frac{b-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =6$ and $\sigma =3.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(7.26<X<8.85) & =P(\frac{7.26-6}{3}<Z<\frac{8.85-6}{3}) \\  & =P(0.42<Z<0.95).\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14263116/assets/39f9ac74ed4f39708f882116edb554b15051ea820e4b5ea8a38e5451ed706251.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.42<Z<0.95) & =P(Z<0.95)-P(Z\le 0.42) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.95)-P(Z\le 0.42) \\  & =Φ(0.95)-Φ(0.42).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.95) & =0.8289 \\ Φ(0.42) & =0.6628\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.42<Z<0.95) & =Φ(0.95)-Φ(0.42) \\  & =0.8289-0.6628 \\  & =0.1661.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(7.26<X<8.85)=0.1661.
$$
